subject: Service obligation audit: metrics, alerting, and partial dashboard onboarding
messages:
From: Sasha Petrov <sasha@nebula.finance>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial procurement questions — how you measure uptime/latency

Hi Evelyn,

Quick context: Nebula Finance is running a vendor audit ahead of our Q4 PCard approval. Our security and SRE teams need to understand a few concrete things about how Redwood measures and exposes service-level commitments. We are primarily focused on inference availability and 95th/99th percentile latency for text-generation endpoints.

Could you confirm the following and return any artifacts (diagram or short spec) you can share?

  - How does Redwood define "uptime" for hosted inference (what endpoints, what traffic counts as healthy)?
  - Which percentiles are tracked (p50/p95/p99) and what measurement window and sampling methodology do you use?
  - Where are metrics hosted and how do customers get access (Grafana links, read-only dashboards, API dumps)?
  - What alerting thresholds and notification channels do you provide for customer-facing incidents?
  - What retention windows and exports are available for audit purposes?

We understand some data is sensitive — if there are short-term exceptions or partial visibility options you can offer during our procurement window, please call those out. I attached the standard vendor questionnaire as XLSX for your convenience.

Thanks,
Sasha Petrov
Vendor Operations — Nebula Finance
procurement@nebula.finance
(415) 555-0192

Attachment: nebula-request-form.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Petrov <sasha@nebula.finance>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-16T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial procurement questions — how you measure uptime/latency

Hi Sasha — thanks for the clear list and the questionnaire. Looping in Marissa (solutions) and Karthik (product) so we can provide a concise evidence packet.

High-level answers below; we will follow up with an artifact (SLO spec) and a short call if that helps.

  - Uptime definition: For hosted inference we define availability as the percentage of 5-minute windows where the system can successfully accept and start processing inference requests (HTTP 202/200 as applicable). We exclude scheduled maintenance windows (published in advance) and major region-wide cloud provider outages per our force majeure clause.
  - Percentiles & sampling: We track p50, p95, and p99 tail latency on request-to-first-byte (RTFB) and p99 for error rate. Measurement uses rolling one-hour windows aggregated into a 30-day reporting window for contractual SLOs; operational alerts use 5m and 1h windows with adaptive thresholds.
  - Customer access: Customers can get read-only Grafana dashboard links, daily timeseries exports (CSV/JSON), and a metrics API for archived exports. For procurement, we can provide a temporary read-only dashboard invite limited to specific IP ranges or SSO groups.
  - Alerting: We publish the on-call escalation path; customers can subscribe to incident webhooks, PagerDuty integrations, and email/SMS notifications for major incidents.
  - Retention: Rolling 90-day high-resolution metrics (1s-1m granularity), 12 months of 5m-15m aggregated metrics; exports available on request for audit (via secure S3 link).

I've attached our SLO spec (redwood-slo-spec-v1.pdf) that lays out measurement definitions and a sample dashboard layout. Marissa — can you add notes on the temp-dashboard invite process and any constraints? Karthik — any product caveats we should flag for procurement?

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
T: (650) 555-0106

Attachments: redwood-slo-spec-v1.pdf (PDF, 72KB); nebula-request-form.xlsx (received)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-17T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial procurement questions — how you measure uptime/latency

Hi Sasha — quick follow-up with a practical onboarding plan we typically offer customers in Nebula's position: 

  1) Evidence packet: SLO spec (attached), sample 30-day export, and a short runbook describing incident lifecycle.
  2) Temporary visibility: We can provision a read-only Grafana link scoped to Nebula for 30 days. If you need SSO access, we'll require an IdP metadata file and an allowed user list; otherwise we can lock to your IP ranges.
  3) Alerting Integration: We'll send a test webhook and provide a sample PagerDuty key integration.
  4) Exceptions: For procurement deadlines we can enable a temporary exception for metrics visibility (no production writes) that expires automatically. Any exception is logged and time-limited; we mark that in the contract addendum.

Ask: Please confirm whether you prefer SSO or IP-restricted access, and which email address we should invite for the dashboard. Also — we can schedule a 30-minute call with our SRE to walk through the dashboards and export formats. Available slots: 2027-08-18 09:00-11:00 PT or 2027-08-18 14:00-16:00 PT.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
